name: IN-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+18 district lean makes this one of the most Republican seats on the 2026 ballot
Incumbent Mark Messmer holds a roughly four-to-one fundraising advantage over Mary Allen
Prediction markets price a Republican win at about 96-97%
No polls, expert ratings, or outside spending signal any competition
model.rationale: The district's R+18 lean, Messmer's incumbency and four-to-one fundraising edge, and markets pricing his win odds near 96% all point the same direction, and no polling or ratings offer any evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: A heavy Democratic midterm wave or the first public polling showing Messmer well below 60% would be the earliest sign the race could tighten.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 8th District is deeply Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly eighteen points toward the GOP. First-term incumbent Mark Messmer is seeking re-election and holds a commanding financial advantage, having raised about $1.17 million to Democrat Mary Allen's roughly $295,000. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race, and prediction markets give Messmer about a 96% chance of winning.

The fundamentals leave little room for an upset. The district's strong Republican tilt, the incumbent's money edge, and the absence of any polling or outside spending suggesting competition all point the same way. A strong Democratic national environment could narrow the margin somewhat, but flipping this seat would require a shift far beyond anything in the current evidence.
